//: WHY THIS USES builds/routes INSTEAD OF THE MODERN rewrites KEY.
Vercel's zero-config detection sees a `public/` directory and concludes the
project is a static site: it publishes public/ to the CDN and never builds
the function. Every server route then returns Vercel's own 404 because the
request never reaches Express, and the dashboard loads WITHOUT its password
prompt because express's auth middleware is never in the path either.
Declaring `builds` switches zero-config off entirely, which is exactly what
this project wants: server/index.js already serves public/ itself (behind
auth), so Vercel must not serve it separately. One route sends everything
to the Express app and it does its own routing, identically to running it
includeFiles is required for public/: @vercel/node traces require() calls
to decide what to bundle, and express.static reads that folder at runtime
rather than requiring it, so it would otherwise be missing from the deploy.
